claim: Some forms of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia were previously viewed as being due to defects in a single RNA-binding protein.
source: New analyses shift the view that some forms of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia are due to defects in a single RNA-binding protein.
evidence: The statement implies that there was a prior view that these diseases were caused by defects in a single RNA-binding protein, which is now being challenged by new analyses.

source: New analyses shift the view that some forms of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia are due to defects in a single RNA-binding protein.
evidence: The abstract directly states that new analyses have changed the prevailing view about the molecular mechanism of these diseases.
